title: Infix to Postfix Converter
description: Convert infix expressions to postfix (Reverse Polish) notation with the shunting-yard algorithm, showing every step: token actions, operator stack and output queue.
howto: Press Convert to run the shunting-yard algorithm.
Read the step table: each token, what the algorithm did with it, the operator stack and the output so far.
Copy the final postfix expression from the result box.

faqs.a: Postfix (Reverse Polish) notation puts operators after their operands, e.g. 3 4 + instead of 3 + 4. It needs no parentheses and is how stack-based calculators evaluate expressions.
The converter uses ^ (highest, right-associative), then * and /, then + and - (left-associative). Parentheses override precedence as usual.
Yes — a minus sign at the start of the expression, after an opening parenthesis, or after another operator is treated as a negative number, e.g. -3 + 4.
